nodes.text: And Trypho, somewhat indignant but showing reverence for the Scriptures, as was plain from his face, said to me: The words of God are holy, but your interpretations are contrived, as is evident also from those you have expounded, or rather they are even blasphemous; for you say that angels did wickedly and revolted from God.

And I, in a gentler tone of voice, wishing to dispose him to listen to me, answered, saying: I admire this reverence of yours, sir, and I pray that you may have the same disposition also toward him whom the angels are written to serve, as Daniel says, that one like a son of man is brought to the Ancient of Days, and to him is given all kingdom for ever and ever [Dan. 7:13–14]. But so that you may know, sir, I said, that it was not by any daring of our own that we made this interpretation [fol. 134] which you blame, I will give you testimony from Isaiah himself, that he says evil angels have dwelt and still dwell also in Tanis, in the land of Egypt.

For by the very name of this Son of God and firstborn of all creation [cf. Col. 1:15], who was born through a virgin and became a man subject to suffering, and was crucified under Pontius Pilate by your people and died, and rose from the dead and ascended into heaven, every demon, when exorcised, is overcome and subjected.

But if you exorcise by any name of those who have arisen among you, whether kings or righteous men or prophets or patriarchs, not one of the demons will be subjected; but if any of you were to exorcise by the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, it will perhaps be subjected. Yet already, I said, your exorcists, using the craft just as the gentiles do, perform exorcisms, and use fumigations and binding spells.
